To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
different analogs of 25‐(OH)-D3 and 1,25-(OH)2D have differential effects on the rapid stimulation of Ca2+ absorption from the intestinal lumen into the epithelial cell.
1, 25‐(OH)(2)D(3) analogs with different affinites for the classic nuclear vitamin D receptor (VDR) initiate the transcaltachia response in chick intestine.
different structural features of 1, 25‐(OH)(2)D(3) analogs are essential for initiating rapid transcaltachia and for binding to the nuclear receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of action of 1,24‐(OH)D3 and its analogs.
the molecular mechanism of the nongemonic pathway of 1, 25‐(OH), D3.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of transcaltachic responses to 1,25(OH)2D3 and its analogs, which are mediated by nongenomic mechanisms, in contrast to the classic genomic pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the classic nuclear receptor and the transcaltachia receptor are not the same.
the rapid stimulation of Ca2+ absorption (transcaldachia) is mediated by an entirely different receptor than that of the classic nuclear 25‐(OH2D3) receptor.
the classic receptor for 1,25(OH)2D3 does not appear to be involved in the transcaltachia response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the classic nuclear receptor for 1,25(OH)2D3 and the membrane receptor(s) for transcaltachia are distinct and that the latter receptor(s) is (are) more sensitive to the presence of the 1‐hydroxyl group of the secosteroid than is the classic receptor.
there are at least three different 1,25(OH)2D3 receptors, each of which is differentially sensitive to the analogs tested.

the nongenomically activated response of transcaltacha, which is mediated by the rapid stimulation of Ca2+ channel opening in the intestinal brush border membrane, is initiated by a different receptor for 1,25 (OH)2D than the classic nuclear vitamin D receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rapid stimulation of calcium transport by 1,25D3 is mediated by a different receptor than the classic nuclear vitamin D receptor.
there are at least two distinct vitamin D receptors, a classic nuclear receptor and a nongenomic membrane receptor.
the classic nuclear receptor for 1,25-(OH)2D is not involved in the rapid stimulation of calcium transport.
